instruction: List all files in the "/tmp/test_files" directory tree that were last modified 30 days ago and save the output to "/tmp/old_files_list.txt"

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

metadata.explanation: Task requires listing files modified 30 days ago and saving to /tmp/old_files_list.txt. Verification reads the file content and checks it includes old_file1.txt and old_file2.txt but excludes new_file1.txt and new_file2.txt. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric with vm_command_line getter.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads output file /tmp/old_files_list.txt using cat command
Metric check_include_exclude correctly verifies include/exclude patterns in the result
Evaluator only checks final output content but cannot verify the core requirement: that files were actually modified 30 days ago
Verification relies entirely on setup.sh creating files with correct modification times without validating this assumption
Time-dependent verification (30 days ago) is fragile - evaluation time vs setup time mismatch could cause false negatives
Does not verify that search was recursive (directory tree) or that expected files actually exist in /tmp/test_files
Evaluator checks symptoms (presence of filenames) rather than actual requirement (modification time filter)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add verification that old_file1.txt and old_file2.txt actually have modification times ~30 days ago using stat command
Add verification that new_file1.txt and new_file2.txt have different modification times (not 30 days ago)
Consider using relative time verification (e.g., files modified between 29-31 days ago) to handle timing variations
Add check that files listed in output actually exist in /tmp/test_files directory tree
Consider verifying the find command logic used by checking file count or using stat to validate modification times
